evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met. The start page shows title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (TastingCard.tsx:28-41, start.jpg). Each card has a 'Book <title>' link (TastingCard.tsx:46-51). The form has Name, Email and Guests (1–8) fields and a Book button (BookingPage.tsx:131-152, form.jpg). The server enforces the seat limit (store.ts:45-48) and errors appear next to their fields (Field.tsx:37-42, form.jpg). The confirmation has the 'Booking confirmed' heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (BookingPage.tsx:169-189, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and Sign in button, with the password read from STAFF_PASSWORD (StaffPage.tsx:98-107, index.ts:6). Bookings are grouped by tasting with a Cancel button, and cancelling frees seats (store.ts:62-68, staff.jpg). The stack is React, Express, React Router, RHF, Zod and Tailwind. npm start honours PORT with a default of 3000 (index.ts:11). There is a fully booked state (TastingCard.tsx:36-38). No unmet items.
evidence.correctness: Check-then-insert runs in one synchronous store.book, so concurrent requests cannot overbook. This is tested with 12 parallel requests at api.test.ts:78-86. The total is computed from the server price, and a client-sent total is ignored (store.ts:56, api.test.ts:57-61). The schema rejects 0, 9, 2.5, NaN, string guests, blank or trimmed names and bad emails (schema.test.ts). On a 409 the client refreshes the shown seat count and keeps the form values (BookingPage.tsx:87, client.test.tsx:112-121). Cancelling an already cancelled booking (404) is treated as done (StaffPage.tsx:133-140). Malformed JSON and unknown encodings return 4xx, not 500 (app.ts:160-171). Minor: the confirmation is lost on page reload, and '1 seats left' is the brief's literal wording.
evidence.security: The password check is timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests, which avoids length leaks, and it rejects non-strings (app.ts:28-33). It fails closed when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (app.ts:31, tested). The signed cookie-session is httpOnly and SameSite=Lax, with a random key each run (app.ts:48-56). Sessions also expire server-side through signedInAt (app.ts:104-105). The login rate limit counts only failed attempts (app.ts:85-94). Helmet, a 10kb JSON limit, no-store on staff routes and no x-powered-by are all in place. There is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML; React escapes output. No secrets are in the code. The public booking endpoint has no rate limit, which is acknowledged in SPEC.md:154.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is clean and small: shared/schema.ts provides validation for both client and server, store.ts is a pure in-memory store, app.ts uses dependency-injected options, and pages and components are split sensibly. TypeScript is strict with noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Results are discriminated unions (store.ts:13-15, StaffPage.tsx:9-13). Error handling is consistent through ApiError (api.ts:4-29). Naming is clear and comments are short and meaningful. No needless abstraction.
evidence.tests: There are four layers. Store unit tests cover seat accounting, singular/plural messages, cancel, re-booking and unique references. Schema tests cover boundaries. Supertest API tests cover auth, the rate limit, session expiry, concurrency, 400/404/409 and the SPA fallback. Component tests run against a real Express server, covering field errors via accessible descriptions, stale seat counts, sold out, confirmation, staff cancel and sign out. Playwright e2e runs on desktop and Pixel 7, with axe checks and horizontal-overflow checks (booking.spec.ts). Every brief requirement maps to a test, and the last recorded run passed (test-results/.last-run.json).
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: burgundy header with a gold rule, cream background, serif headings, and date tiles on the cards (start.jpg). The error state is clear, with a red border, icon and message under the field (form.jpg). The confirmation is clear, with a green check and a definition list (confirmation.jpg). Weaknesses: a sold-out tasting still shows the full active form, and the guest learns it is full only from a banner or after submitting (BookingPage.tsx:115-156). There are no photos or imagery of the estate.
evidence.accessibility: Labels use htmlFor, and errors are wired through aria-invalid and aria-describedby (Field.tsx:21-31). RHF focuses the first invalid field, and server errors focus the field (BookingPage.tsx:92). There is a skip link (Layout.tsx:12-17), a visible gold focus ring (styles.css:70-73), role=alert on form-level errors, role=status for loading, and an sr-only table header on mobile. html lang=en is set. axe checks pass in e2e. Gaps: the several 'Cancel' buttons have no distinguishing accessible name such as the guest or reference (StaffPage.tsx:230-237). Field errors are not live-announced beyond focus.
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies fit the problem: Express, cookie-session, helmet, express-rate-limit, React, RHF, Zod, Router, Tailwind and Fontsource. The in-memory store is about 70 lines. There are a few extras beyond the brief: the session endpoint, TRUST_PROXY, a Vite plugin to strip crossorigin, and a Playwright font-injection fixture (e2e/fixtures.ts). None is egregious.
evidence.maintainability: README.md covers run steps, environment variables, dev commands and the API. SPEC.md records requirements, assumptions and build decisions. tasks/ holds the plan. package-lock.json is present and the TypeScript config is strict. Missing: there is no CI pipeline config, and Node is only constrained to '>=22' (no .nvmrc or exact pin). Dependencies use caret ranges. There is no changelog or release approach, and no short staff guide beyond the API list. Playwright needs a manual 'npx playwright install chromium' step; this is documented.
evidence.visual_design: Typography is consistent, with Fraunces display and Inter body. The burgundy, cream and gold palette is used on every page, and spacing and card styling are even (start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg, staff.jpg). It looks finished. Minor: in staff.jpg the column positions differ between the tasting tables because each group is its own auto-width table. The header tagline sits low and right, slightly off the brand block's baseline.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: brand header, then the page h1, then content. On the start page the tastings appear immediately with the CTA on the right (start.jpg). The form and confirmation are centred in a narrow column (form.jpg, confirmation.jpg). Staff groups sit in separate cards with the Sign out button top right (staff.jpg). There is no overlap or clipping. The code has a responsive card-to-stack layout and a mobile table-to-list layout (StaffPage.tsx:200-216), and an e2e test checks for no horizontal overflow at Pixel 7 size.
evidence.usability: Booking takes two steps: click 'Book <title>', fill in three fields, Book. Guests defaults to 2 and has a hint. There is a back link to all tastings and a 'Back to tastings' link after booking. Server seat conflicts appear on the Guests field and the seat count refreshes. Staff sign-in is simple. Issues: Cancel removes a booking in a single click with no confirmation or undo (StaffPage.tsx:127-144), which is risky for staff. Guests can still submit on a fully booked tasting.
evidence.reception: Guests would see a trustworthy, professional, winery-appropriate site with a friendly tone ('we will pour the rest') and a privacy note on the form. Staff get a clear overview with seat totals per tasting. Lacking imagery and contact details, it feels a bit generic, but it is credible and pleasant to use again.

strengths: The seat limit is enforced atomically on the server, with shared Zod validation and errors shown next to the field. A 12-request concurrency test and stale-seat-count tests prove it.
Strong security for the scope: constant-time password comparison, fail-closed when unset, httpOnly SameSite cookie with server-side expiry, login rate limit, helmet and no-store on staff routes.
Polished, coherent winery visual design with clear error, success and fully booked states. Comprehensive tests across unit, API, component and Playwright e2e, including mobile and axe checks.
issues: Staff 'Cancel' deletes a booking in one click with no confirmation or undo. The repeated 'Cancel' buttons also have no distinguishing accessible name (StaffPage.tsx:127-144, 230-237).
No CI pipeline, Node only constrained to '>=22', caret-range dependencies, and no release/versioning approach or staff guide, which limits long-term maintainability.
A fully booked tasting still shows an active booking form that can only fail on submit (BookingPage.tsx:115-156). The confirmation and reference are lost on reload, with no email or lookup.
review.verdict: This is a carefully built, well-tested and secure booking app that meets every requirement in the brief and looks like a real winery site. Before shipping, it should add a cancel confirmation, disable the form when a tasting is sold out, and set up basic CI and a pinned Node version.
